answer: Scanners at each harbor intake read one velvet seal at a time, and that sequential reading is the bottleneck a farm cannot widen. Each identity bonds a velvet strip, its random fibres hashed, over a token holding 30 units locked for 20 epochs. The station publishes each scan hash; any pattern under two identities is a public duplicate proof, and both fall to a nadir of zero weight while the 30 are slashed. An honest agent buys one strip for 12 units yearly and waits 3 minutes; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 strips, 30,000 units locked, and 50 scanner-hours that cannot run in parallel on one line.
